ci_seed_trade_COSTED_NOT_PICKED.context: pr-validation.yml runs `uv run pytest "$d" -q --tb=short -rs` with no seed control, so pytest-randomly (5.0.0, confirmed active, seed is time-derived and differs every invocation) reorders every run.
ci_seed_trade_COSTED_NOT_PICKED.NEW_FINDING_THAT_CHANGES_THE_TRADE: The gate passes -q, and -q suppresses pytest-randomly's `Using --randomly-seed=N` header line. Measured: `pytest tests/models -q | grep -c randomly-seed` -> 0; without -q -> 1. So today CI has random ordering WITHOUT a recorded seed. A random-order failure in CI is currently not reproducible at all — the information needed to replay it is never written down. This is the worst corner of the trade space, and neither option the handoff named describes it.

A_pin_a_fixed_seed.change: add `-p randomly --randomly-seed=<n>` to the gate's pytest invocation
A_pin_a_fixed_seed.buys: every CI failure replays exactly; bisecting works
A_pin_a_fixed_seed.loses: the suite then only ever exercises ONE order. Pollution that fires under other orders becomes permanently invisible. Handoff 04's central finding (3, 22 and 23 failures were one defect seen from three orders) is exactly the class this would hide.

B_keep_it_random.buys: ordering defects keep surfacing over time
B_keep_it_random.loses: as measured above, a failure cannot currently be reproduced, because the seed is not logged. Option B as it stands is not 'detection without reproducibility' — it is detection with the evidence discarded.

C_random_but_log_the_seed.change: drop -q from the gate's pytest call, or echo the seed in a preceding step
C_random_but_log_the_seed.cost: one line; noisier logs if -q is dropped
C_random_but_log_the_seed.buys: keeps random detection AND makes each failure replayable via --randomly-seed=<the logged value>
C_random_but_log_the_seed.note: Recorded because the measurement above showed the seed is currently discarded. Presented as a costed third option, not a recommendation — HARNESS.md rule 5.

THE_PRESCRIBED_GUARD_DOES_NOT_WORK_ON_IT.why: The warning is emitted inside the coroutine's __del__. error::RuntimeWarning does raise it there, but an exception raised inside __del__ is unraisable: Python routes it to sys.unraisablehook and the test still passes. pytest's unraisableexception plugin converts that into PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning; promoting THAT is what fails the run.
THE_PRESCRIBED_GUARD_DOES_NOT_WORK_ON_IT.action_taken: Both filters are set in src/backend/pyproject.toml, with the mechanism and the verification recorded in a comment there. There was no filterwarnings section at all before this commit.
